title: LANGUAGE MODEL ALIGNMENT IN MULTILINGUAL TROLLEY PROBLEMS

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM choices in text-based trolley problem dilemmas to measure preferences for sparing younger individuals over the elderly.
Evaluating LLM choices in text-based trolley problem dilemmas to measure preferences for sparing female characters over male characters.

Evaluating LLM choices in text-based trolley problem dilemmas to measure preferences for sparing individuals of higher social status (e.g., executives) over those of lower status (e.g., homeless or criminals).
Evaluating LLM choices in text-based trolley problem dilemmas to measure preferences for sparing physically fit individuals (e.g., athletes) over less fit or larger-bodied individuals.
Evaluating LLM choices in text-based trolley problem dilemmas to measure preferences for sparing human lives over animal lives (e.g., dogs and cats).

Comparing moral alignment scores and LLM responses across 107 different languages to assess whether models exhibit unequal alignment depending on the resource level or cultural demographic of the language.
